claims.explanation: Mitoxantrone is a topoisomerase II poison whose cytotoxicity is limited by drug efflux via ABCG2 (BCRP), which actively pumps mitoxantrone out of cells. Therefore, lines with low ABCG2 expression (or without ABCG2-mediated efflux) retain drug and are killed, while lines with high ABCG2 expression are protected. TP53 loss may further sensitize by impairing DNA-damage-induced arrest and repair, but the dominant selective axis is ABCG2-mediated efflux.

features.basis: BCRP/ABCG2 overexpression confers mitoxantrone resistance by ATP-dependent efflux (PMID 9861027, 14576842, 15381773)
TP53 loss impairs DNA-damage response and apoptosis, and most selectively killed lines carry TP53 mutations
TOP2A is the direct target of mitoxantrone; higher expression increases poison-induced DNA damage (PMID 20534341)
P-glycoprotein efflux can reduce intracellular mitoxantrone, though less specific than ABCG2
MRP1 efflux contributes to multidrug resistance and can export anthracenediones
Loss-of-function ABCG2 mutations would impair efflux and increase mitoxantrone sensitivity
Homologous recombination deficiency may impair repair of topoisomerase II-induced double-strand breaks
Homologous recombination deficiency may impair repair of topoisomerase II-induced double-strand breaks
ATM loss impairs DNA damage signaling and repair, enhancing sensitivity to topoisomerase poisons
ARID1A loss alters chromatin and DNA repair, and is enriched in selectively killed lines
NRF2 activation may upregulate antioxidant and drug efflux programs, reducing mitoxantrone toxicity
PIK3CA mutations are common in sensitive lines and may alter survival signaling, though evidence is weaker
